declined.reason: Standardised the first magazine title to *Kōdan Club*, with macron and italics, as the bible requires; a wholesale respelling of every kōza/koza occurrence was not carried through this pass, and the remaining inconsistency is flagged below rather than silently claimed as fixed. Outside p2 the text was left as drafted, so this note is only partly answered.

Declined: 響く is a sound word in the Japanese ('rang pleasant in him'); the suggested 'felt it warm in him' warms and clarifies a metaphor the text leaves as sound, which is the kind of tidying the reading warns against. The English is stiff, but stiff in the direction of the source.

Declined: そのあとはお前の世界にしてやるから is kept literal ('I will make it your world') because Takami does in fact hand him the floor later; glossing it in-line as 'your turn, your stage' explains in the text what the evening itself goes on to show.

Declined: the triple 'part' (役 … 一役 … 役) is the flat reported texture of the host's paraphrase, which the reading requires be kept flat and a little long-winded; smoothing it to 'just the tiger, nothing but the tiger' polishes the paraphrase into a line.

Declined the added lineation: the source runs the cat-fight, the gloss and the failed Hachi turn in one paragraph of reported performance, and breaking it into stage beats would make a set piece of what must stay a man describing a flop to a room that stays prim.

Declined the suggested wording, which switches the third-person narration into 'I beat my wife'; the admission stands in the text as 'he knocked her about till she spent it all', blunt and at the passage's dogged temperature, and it sits inside dashes because the Japanese sets it inside ―― asides. Not euphemised, and not given a climax either.

Accepted the italic marking of his borrowed *situation* but not 'pull that *situation* stunt': やっては carries no noun, and adding 'stunt' interprets his misuse for the reader instead of leaving it visible.

Accepted that バック must be heard as a loanword, but rendered it simply as *back*, one of the paired sounds he fails to parse at p82; the double rendering 'background — of back —' explains the ruby in the text, which the style sheet forbids.

Accepted that the beranmei shift must be audible, but declined 'Yer don't understand much yerself … neither': the reading forbids broad dialect comedy for Nekohachi outright, since dialect spelling does to him exactly what his audiences do. The shift was marked instead by dropped, blunter syntax ('I've took your gate money already, so you can get off home quick'), and 帰したくねい was corrected to 'send you home'.

disagreements.choice: Took R1 in the one paragraph edited: the run-on, self-interrupting syntax and the appeals are kept, the identical terminal tag is not. This follows the reading's own instruction to render な/でげす by syntax and verbal tics rather than by a repeated tag, and the same principle governs his other speeches without a clause-by-clause rewrite.
disagreements.faithful_side: F-side (and the translator's notes throughout) keeps 'eh' as the standing equivalent of sentence-final な/でげす, so the density of tags in p8 is faithful to the density of the Japanese.
disagreements.readable_side: R1: an 'eh' on almost every clause reads in English as a translator's tic, not as working patter, and flattens his voice into monotony.

disagreements.choice: Marked loanwords in italics where they are being heard or mouthed (p51 *situation*, p67 *situation*, p78 *back*, p82 *back*/*haikei*, p118 *genjitsu-shugi*), and left the group's own critical uses in plain English (background at p80/p87, realism/concrete at p112–p116). The two Englishes stay unmerged, and his misunderstandings are left for the reader to infer, as the open questions in the reading require; no in-text glosses were added.
disagreements.faithful_side: F2–F5 and F19: シチュエイション, バック and the hiragana げんじつ主義 reach Nekohachi as foreign sound and must not be flattened into ordinary English, or the language collision that is the action disappears.
disagreements.readable_side: No reader note opposes the marking directly, but the readable interest throughout (R7, R8) is that borrowed terms stay followable for an English reader rather than accumulating as unexplained foreign matter.

disagreements.choice: Took the shared substance and refused both proposed wordings: no dialect spelling (against F18), no 'wooden gate charge' (with R8). Kept his polite frame, dropped into short blunt syntax for the heckle, unified 木戸銭 as 'gate money' at p153 and p161, and corrected the sense of 帰したくねい. The reading settles the form — dropped, self-interrupting colloquial syntax, never stage dialect — so this does not go up.
disagreements.faithful_side: F18: the shift from わたくし to おめえさん/おいら is a marked change of voice and is invisible in the draft's uniform polite English; F18's own remedy is respelt dialect ('Yer don't understand much yerself').
disagreements.readable_side: R8: the shift is lost at the same temperature as his polite patter and 'wooden gate charge' stops the act cold; R8's remedy is jabbing syntax and lineation, not dialect spelling.

disagreements.choice: Left the text as it stands ('As for customers' feet, I'm seasoned to rubbing little sticks, you know'). Neither reader could supply the sense, the translator's note already leaves it literal and clumsy rather than smoothed, and inventing a yose-clappers image to fill the gap would break the house's honesty rule. What would settle it: a period-dictionary or yose-usage check on 摺り小木 in this collocation with お客の足, and whether it is wordplay needing one sparse note.
disagreements.faithful_side: F12: the phrase is rendered as literal nonsense; F12 is unsure what 摺り小木 means here (worn pestle? being inured? a joke?) and asks for a period check, leaving the gap visible until then.
disagreements.readable_side: R5: as English it is incomprehensible — no reader can see what rubbing little sticks has to do with customers' feet — and it may need a sparse note rather than an in-text gloss.

disagreements.choice: Left the draft's variation (fall / ochi / conclusion) untouched in this pass and sent the choice up, because the house's open questions already reserve how far his borrowed and misapplied terms are to be regularised, and a wrong regularisation here would run through p64, p82, p85–p87, p104, p154–p155. What would settle it: an editorial ruling on one English set for 落ち (ochi kept in roman after one gloss, or 'fall' throughout) against the bible's 'keep ochi as fall/punchline glossed once if needed'.
disagreements.faithful_side: The translator's notes defend 'fall' as the standing rendering that holds his rakugo expectation without explaining rakugo, with ochi itself kept at p154.
disagreements.readable_side: R7: the term is varied away across the evening as fall, ochi/fall, ochi, conclusion, so an English reader cannot follow that he keeps asking for the same rakugo thing — the repetition is a load-bearing network and elegant variation dissolves it.

disagreements.choice: Left the literal rendering standing. The Japanese is a gnomic shrug whose exact scope the translator's note already flags as uncertain; replacing it with 'worrying himself sick' would settle a resignation the sentence does not quite state. What would settle it: confirmation of the idiom's force in period usage (fretting oneself over something pointless) and whether the house wants it Englished or left as his flat literalism.
disagreements.faithful_side: No faithful note on the span; the translator's note reads it as his gnomic shrug that no one frets himself for nothing and deliberately leaves the belly-ache wording visible rather than smoothing it.
disagreements.readable_side: R11: 'nobody would needlessly give himself a stomach-ache' means nothing in English and the closing paragraph drifts; 腹を痛める likely means fretting/worrying oneself sick.

data.say:
Edits made (each a separate edit call, smallest form): F1 — 廃兵院 unified as 'Veterans' Home' at p62, p127–p128, p175, p181 and p186, replacing Soldiers' Home / Haiheiin / veterans' hospital / Invalids Home / Disabled Veterans' Hospital, so the institution–woods repetition network holds. F6 — 'something cries Father' → 'someone cries 'Father' and flings himself upon him' (p87). F7 — the stare at p91 made a performed one ('made a show of opening his eyes wide'). F8 — 'He knew well enough himself' → 'He could not say he did not know himself' (p91). F9 — p161 re-subjected so Nekohachi does the looking and the leaver fails to notice. F10 — 'my side' → 'his side' (p152). F11 — 'like people in our trade' → 'like us' (p13). F13 — the completed denial at p71 → 'But as for me, a thing like that —'. F14 — 'in that fix' → 'in that case' (p69). F16 — p124 → 'keeping his face deadpan, giving nothing away, he went hohokekyo.' F17 — the doubled zero at p141 reduced to one. F15 — p123 → 'Now, from here on this was at last my world, he thought,' keeping the slide into おれ. Loanwords marked: *situation* p51 and p67, *back* p78, *back*/*haikei* p82, *genjitsu-shugi* p118. F18/R8 — p153 rewritten in dropped blunt syntax without dialect spelling, 木戸銭 unified as 'gate money' there and at p161. R1 — p8 recast into run-on self-interrupting patter without an 'eh' on every clause. R2 (first occurrence only) — 'Koudan Club' → '*Kōdan Club*'. Notes taken without separate entry above: F2, F5, F6, F7, F8, F9, F10, F11, F13, F14, F15, F16, F17, F19, R8.

Declined, each with its reason, and disagreements and unsettled points with both sides, my choice and whether they go up, are listed in the structured fields. The three sent up are p33 (摺り小木), the 落ち terminology set, and p186; the p153 disagreement is settled by the reading and does not go up. Nothing in this part showed anything that changes how an earlier part should read.

House log: The desk held the two registers apart — loanwords marked as heard sound, Nekohachi's patter kept in syntax rather than tags or dialect — unified the Veterans' Home and gate-money repetitions, restored his half-knowing performed grief at p91, and sent up the suri-kogi phrase, the ochi word-set and the closing stomach-ache idiom unsettled.
